regulation_full_name: Federal Reserve Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
clause_title: Model development, implementation, and use — purpose, theory, and design
clause_text: An effective development process begins with a clear statement of purpose to ensure that model development is aligned with the intended use. The design, theory, and logic underlying the model should be well documented and generally supported by published research and sound industry practice. The model methodologies and processing components that implement the theory, including the mathematical specification and the numerical techniques and approximations, should be explained in detail with particular attention to merits and limitations.

regulation_full_name: Federal Reserve Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
clause_text: Ongoing monitoring confirms that the model is appropriately implemented and is being used and is performing as intended. Monitoring is essential to evaluate whether changes in products, exposures, activities, clients, or market conditions necessitate adjustment, redevelopment, or replacement of the model and to verify that any extension of the model beyond its original scope is valid.

regulation_full_name: Federal Reserve Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
clause_text: Effective model validation helps reduce model risk by identifying model errors, corrective actions, and appropriate use. The range and rigor of validation activities should be commensurate with the extent of model risk. Validation involves a degree of independence from model development and use. The procedures should include three core elements: evaluation of conceptual soundness, ongoing monitoring including process verification and benchmarking, and outcomes analysis including back-testing.

regulation_full_name: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
clause_text: Model risk management begins with robust model development, implementation, and use. Banks should have a system in place that ensures effective challenge of models, an objective and qualified party should review the model and offer constructive criticism. Effective challenge depends on a combination of incentives, competence, and influence.

A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems. The risk management system shall consist of a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of the high-risk AI system, including identification and analysis of known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimation and evaluation of risks that may emerge when the system is used in accordance with its intended purpose and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse, and evaluation of other risks possibly arising based on the analysis of data gathered from the post-market monitoring system.

High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which the AI system is in use. Human oversight shall aim at preventing or minimising the risks to health, safety or fundamental rights. The measures shall enable the individuals to whom human oversight is assigned to correctly interpret the high-risk AI system's output, to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system, and to disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system.

reporting_obligation.trigger: serious incident or malfunction breaching fundamental rights

clause_text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle. The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use. High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates.

clause_title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
clause_text: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions of use accompanying the systems. Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support. Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use and, when relevant, inform providers when they have reasons to consider that the use in accordance with the instructions for use may result in that AI system presenting a risk.

reporting_obligation.regulator: AI system provider + national supervisory authority
reporting_obligation.trigger: use of the AI system presenting a risk to health, safety, or fundamental rights

regulation_full_name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
clause_text: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented. Tasks for AI actors include: deployment of cybersecurity controls appropriate to the risks the AI system poses; deployment of safeguards to mitigate risks of misuse, including manipulation, evasion, and exfiltration attacks; tracking and documentation of incidents related to AI system security and resilience, including issues identified.

regulation_full_name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
clause_text: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override mechanisms, decommissioning processes, and incident response and recovery procedures. Monitoring should detect emerging risks and degraded performance.

regulation_full_name: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook — Information Security (AI/ML supplemental guidance)
clause_text: Financial institutions using AI and machine learning models for risk decisions are expected to apply equivalent oversight controls to those required of traditional models, including documented change management, ongoing performance monitoring, model risk validation independent of development, and clear escalation procedures when monitoring detects deviation from expected behavior.

regulation_full_name: Bank of England / PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 — Model risk management principles for banks
clause_text: Firms should monitor the performance of models on an ongoing basis and review the models periodically to confirm they remain fit for purpose. The frequency and depth of monitoring should be commensurate with the materiality of the model. Monitoring procedures should include tracking model performance against benchmarks and triggering remedial action where performance deviates significantly.

reporting_obligation.trigger: material breach of model performance thresholds

regulation_full_name: FCA Handbook — Supervision Manual, Notifications to the FCA
clause_text: A firm must notify the FCA immediately it becomes aware, or has information which reasonably suggests, that any of the following has occurred, may have occurred or may occur in the foreseeable future: any matter that could have a significant adverse impact on the firm's reputation; any matter that could affect the firm's ability to continue to provide adequate services to its customers; any matter in respect of which the FCA would reasonably expect notice.

reporting_obligation.trigger: any matter that could have a significant adverse impact on the firm's reputation or customer service

clause_title: Reporting suspicious transactions and PEP screening
clause_text: Member States shall require obliged entities and, where applicable, their directors and employees, to cooperate fully by promptly informing the FIU, including by filing a report, on their own initiative, where the obliged entity knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect that funds, regardless of the amount involved, are the proceeds of criminal activity or are related to terrorist financing. PEP screening processes that produce false positives or false negatives at a material rate are themselves a reportable control weakness.

reporting_obligation.trigger: material PEP screening false positive / false negative rate

regulation_full_name: Equal Credit Opportunity Act — Regulation B (12 CFR 1002)
clause_text: A creditor shall not discriminate against an applicant on a prohibited basis regarding any aspect of a credit transaction. Discrimination on a prohibited basis includes treating an applicant less favorably than other applicants on a prohibited basis (disparate treatment) and a policy or practice that has an adverse impact on the basis of a prohibited factor (disparate impact), unless the policy or practice meets a legitimate business need that cannot reasonably be achieved by means that are less disparate in their impact.
